question.text: The correct order of equivalent conductances at infinite dilution in water at room temperature for $\mathrm{H}^{+}, \mathrm{K}^{+}, \mathrm{CH}_{3} \mathrm{COO}^{-}$ and $\mathrm{HO}^{-}$ ions is

solution.text: Equivalent conductance $\left(\Lambda_{\mathrm{eq}}\right)$ is defined as the conducting power of all the ions produced by one gram equivalent of an electrolyte in a given solution.in case of weak electrolytes (as $\mathrm{CH}_{3} \mathrm{COOH}, \mathrm{NH}_{4} \mathrm{OH}, \mathrm{AgCl}$ etc. $),$ ionisation is very small compared to strong electrolytes (as KCl, NaOH etc.), hence $\Lambda_{\text {oq }}$ of weak electrolyte is low. Moreover, ionisation of $\mathrm{H}^{*}$ is maximum among given ions. Thus, correct of order of $\Lambda_{\mathrm{eq}}$ is $\mathrm{H}^{+}>\mathrm{OH}^{-}>\mathrm{K}^{+}>\mathrm{CH}_{3} \mathrm{COO}^{-}$
